sources.title: COVID-19 Vaccine: Addressing Concerns - UCLA Health
sources.excerpt: No. There is no way for the COVID-19 vaccine to alter your genetic material (DNA).

reasoning:
According to overwhelming scientific consensus from major health organizations (such as the CDC, WHO, and NIH) and leading medical institutions (such as UCLA Health, Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, and the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia), mRNA COVID-19 vaccines do not and cannot alter or permanently change human DNA. 

The mRNA from the vaccine enters the cytoplasm of the host cell, where ribosomes use it as a template to synthesize the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. It does not enter the cell nucleus, where human DNA is located. Furthermore, human cells lack the specific enzymes required—such as reverse transcriptase (to convert RNA back into DNA) and integrase (to insert foreign DNA into the host genome)—for vaccine mRNA to integrate into or modify human genetic material. Once the spike protein is produced, the cell quickly degrades the vaccine mRNA.
title: mRNA vaccines alter human DNA
